title: Define symbol-ID width and stability grammar

state.decision_rationale: Accepted and completed in MKTCTX/5: symbol ordinals are canonical minimum-three-digit unbounded decimals, explicitly packet-local to analyzer traversal, with S999/S1000 parent, citation, verifier, sidecar, and generated-fixture coverage.

provenance.source_label: Kimi K3 critique: symbol ID overflow
provenance.review_target: MKTCTX/3 Continuum packet; exact artifact not identified

feedback.verbatim: SNNN is 3-wide; a file can exceed 999 symbols. Either use variable width with a declared grammar or SNNNN.
feedback.normalized_claim: The guide and grammar must say whether symbol ordinals are fixed-width or variable-width and must support files with at least 1000 symbols without ambiguity.

current_behavior: The guide describes symbols as Fxxxxxxxxxxxx:SNNN, which visually implies exactly three digits.
The generator uses String(index + 1).padStart(3, "0"), so ordinal 1000 naturally emits S1000 rather than overflowing or wrapping.
Symbol IDs are ordinal within the analyzer-provided per-file symbol traversal and can change when earlier symbols are inserted or analyzer ordering changes.
The formal accepted width and stability scope are not yet normative.
evidence: src/context.test.ts: duplicate symbol names consume distinct jump-table occurrences

proposal.summary: Document symbol IDs as a minimum-three-digit, unbounded decimal ordinal or choose another explicit grammar, and state their packet-local stability guarantees.
candidate_changes: Change the guide notation to Sddd+ or another unambiguous variable-width grammar.
Add tests for S999, S1000, and larger ordinals in records, parent references, edges, and CSV sidecars.
Document whether symbol IDs are packet-local ordinals, stable under content edits, or stable only for identical analyzer output.
Specify maximum supported ordinal limits for parsers, if any.
non_goals: Do not claim that current code fails at symbol 1000; it already emits S1000.
Do not make ordinal symbol IDs globally durable without separately designing content- or structure-derived identity.
Do not increase every small symbol ID to a wider fixed width solely for appearance.

questions: Is minimum width useful, or should leading zeros be removed entirely?
Should durable citations use symbol ordinals, packet identity, content hash, or a combination?
Do any existing consumers validate exactly three digits?
risks: Tightening the grammar may expose incompatible parsers that assumed exactly three digits.
Variable-width lexical sorting differs from numeric sorting after S999.
Clarifying packet-local stability may reveal that current citation examples overstate durability.
evidence_needed: A generated fixture with more than 1000 symbols.
Consumer parser audit for fixed-width assumptions.
Citation-stability experiments across insertions and analyzer-version changes.
